_readme: THRESHOLDS FOR `node tools/perf-audit.mjs --budget`. Exceeding one fails CI.
==> CALIBRATED 2026-09-09 FROM THE RUNNER, NOT GUESSED FROM A MAC. <==
The first version of this file said, in this slot, that its numbers were
placeholders written from a Chrome extension on a Mac and had to be redone
from the first real run. That never happened, and the gate was red every
single night from 21 August to 9 September — 25 runs, zero passes. A budget
nobody can pass gets switched off, and this one was three weeks into
becoming exactly that.
The numbers below come from the eight runs recorded on the `perf-history`
branch, warm-sw arm, throttled. Observed on 8 Sep: 213 modules in 4 waves,
603 ms staircase, serial depth 2, 206 KB transferred, 3 radar tiles on pan.
Each ceiling sits above the observed value by enough that runner variance
does not trip it and little enough that a real regression does.
`armUnderBudget` is `warm-sw` deliberately: 1,991 of 2,036 D1 sessions are
service-worker controlled, so that is the path worth defending.
==> A null IS NOT A DISABLED CHECK. <== It means the tool measures and
prints the number and cannot fail on it, because nobody has yet seen enough
runs of it to know what normal looks like. Every null here is a debt: read
it off the next few nightly runs and replace it with a figure in a reviewed
commit. Same convention as `tools/perf-budgets.json`.
==> `ourModules` IS THE ONE THAT WILL CREEP. <== It went 179 → 189 → 204 →
209 → 213 across three weeks of recorded runs. There is no build step by
design, so every module is a request every visitor makes, and the count only
ever goes one way on its own. 240 is a ceiling with room to work in, not a
target to grow into. When it trips, the answer is a look at the import
graph, not a bigger number here.
==> `blockedMs` WAS THE SECOND REASON THIS GATE COULD NEVER GO GREEN. <==
It summed long tasks across the whole 14-second settle window, so it
included roughly twelve seconds of a drifting globe being redrawn in
software on a runner with no GPU at 4x CPU throttle. It read 13,915–27,330
ms against a threshold of 1,200 that plainly meant the LOAD. The tool now
splits the window; `blockedLoadMs` is the half worth defending and it starts
as a null because this change is the first run that will ever produce it.
The total stays, also as a null, so the series on `perf-history` is
continuous either side of the split.
==> `colorNulls` WAS RENAMED TO `colorNullsMainThread` ON 2026-08-23, AND
THE BUDGET OF 0 IS NOW KNOWN TO BE UNENFORCEABLE. <== The errors come from
MapLibre's worker, which has its own console that this instrument cannot
reach, so the counter can read 0 while the app emits them the whole time —
which is exactly what happened and was recorded as a pass. The row is kept
rather than deleted so the blind spot stays visible in every report; it is
not a check that can currently fail, and it must not be read as one.
